title: Warm Lentil Salad
subtitle: Puy lentils with mustard vinaigrette and herbs
excerpt: Puy lentils hold their shape when cooked and absorb dressing well while still warm. This salad uses a sharp mustard and red wine vinegar dressing, which the lentils soak up beautifully. It works as a main course or a side dish and is good at any temperature.
sourceNotes: A classic of French bistro cooking. Puy lentils from Le Puy-en-Velay in France have protected designation of origin status. The warm lentil salad is a staple of French home and restaurant cooking.

recipe.batchNotes: Lentils keep in the fridge for 4 days. Dress fresh portions as needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the lentils ahead. Dress while still warm before serving.

content.text: Do not salt the cooking water until the lentils are nearly tender. Salt added too early keeps the lentils firm. Drain them while still slightly al dente -- they will soften further as they absorb the dressing.

items.prepNote: roughly chopped, for cooking the lentils

content.text: Put the lentils in a saucepan with the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, and thyme. Cover with cold water by 5cm. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until just tender.
Season with salt for the last 5 minutes of cooking. Drain. Remove the aromatics.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar, and olive oil into a dressing. Season.
Toss the warm lentils with the dressing and parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.fix: Check frequently after 18 minutes and drain as soon as they are just tender.
Always dress lentils while they are still hot.

content.text: Warm lentil salad is a staple of French bistro cooking. Puy lentils -- the small, slate-green variety from the Auvergne -- are prized for their firm texture and nutty flavour. They have been grown in the Le Puy region for centuries and now carry a protected designation of origin. This salad is often served alongside sausages or grilled meat, but works well as a main course too.
